summary: The simulation code is syntactically correct, imports are appropriate, and the implementation provides a coherent agent-based adoption model with media, policy, market access, enforcement, and optional SEIR-lite disease dynamics. It adheres to the special requirement of calling main() at global scope. Only minor style and potential UX/performance considerations were found.

issues.description: Unnecessary 'pass' statements appear in many functions and classes before the actual implementation. They are harmless but add noise.
issues.location: Multiple functions and class bodies (e.g., clamp, safe_div, sigmoid, Person, Location, Government, Media, Retailer, etc.)
issues.solution: Remove the redundant 'pass' statements to improve code clarity.

issues.description: DATA_DIR is computed from environment variables but never used.
issues.location: Top of file where PROJECT_ROOT and DATA_PATH are read
issues.solution: Either use DATA_DIR where appropriate or remove it along with related environment variables if not needed.

issues.description: Location.observed_norms is computed but not used to influence behavior or metrics.
issues.solution: Either integrate observed_norms into adoption or enforcement logic, or remove it to simplify the code.

issues.description: Daily visitation sets are recomputed in both visits_and_enforcement and disease_step, doubling work.
issues.solution: Compute visits once per day and pass/store them for reuse in disease_step to avoid redundant work.

issues.description: File I/O (save_json and save_results) is not wrapped in try/except; failures will raise and stop the program.
issues.solution: Optionally wrap file operations in try/except and log or report errors gracefully.

issues.description: Direct main() invocation with argparse may parse ambient/unknown CLI arguments in some environments.
issues.location: Global scope call to main() and parse_args()
issues.solution: Given the system requirement to call main() directly, this is acceptable. If needed, consider allowing unknown args via parse_known_args() or isolating arg parsing for embedded contexts.
